post.caption:
A star is a standoff: gravity crushing inward, fusion pushing back exactly hard enough, lasting as long as the fuel does. The counterintuitive part is that bigger stars die sooner, because more mass means more crushing and it has to burn far harder to hold itself up. The largest last a few million years, small red dwarfs will last trillions, and essentially every one ever formed is still burning. Small stars end as white dwarfs. The big ones end all at once.
